concerns.message: theft-loop's '≥60 ticks before choiceDeadline' assertion assumes the e2e server keeps the full 100-tick (5 s) theft window, which leaves 40 world ticks (2 s) from the window opening to the click. The integration suite already uses test-only rule overrides through createLedger({ rules }). If the e2e server path shares those overrides or shortened encounter timings, the window may be under 60 ticks and the assertion can never pass. The 2 s budget also assumes the snapshot's client shows the choice options as soon as the options message arrives. If they wait behind a K.O./result banner or the arena-to-sea transition, the budget is tighter than it looks. Separately, 'server ticks' must mean the ledger's 20 Hz world ticks. The room also has a 60 Hz match clock, and 60 ticks of that clock is 1 s, not 3 s.
concerns.consequence: If any of these assumptions fails, theft-loop either fails every run or fails intermittently on this shared, loaded machine. The browser check then costs a verification attempt (3 max), or the worker weakens the margin to get it green.

concerns.message: In the integration test, the winner must send the type `defaultTheftType` would NOT pick. After the guest collects one of each type, the free-source counts are tied (3 and 3), so the default falls back to the fixed type order. If the test hard-codes 'the second type', a later change to the layout or to who collects what can make the chosen type equal the default. It should compute the default from the room's ledger state (defaultTheftType and eligibleTheftTypes are exported from the objectives index) and assert that the sent type differs from it, as well as asserting settlement.choice === 'winner'.
concerns.consequence: With a hard-coded type, the test can silently stop proving a non-default choice. The coverage reviewer blocks again on the same finding.

concerns.message: Finding 2's invariant assertions can pass without checking anything. The per-tick check runs inside advance(). If a test tears down the room right after the leave, and the quit is handled in onLeave, no tick runs between the ship's removal and the assertion, so `invariantViolations` is empty by default. This matters most in match.test.ts's 'removes a ship when its player leaves' and in admission tests where joins are refused.
concerns.consequence: Vacuous assertions let a regression in the quit path (a ship removed while the ledger still counts its player) through, and the coverage reviewer can flag the finding as not really fixed. The tracker should also assert that it saw at least one tick after the leave.

concerns.message: The seed-privacy test must show that the deal follows the injected source and not the match code. If the worker sends all of the room's randomness through the new seam, including match-code generation, then 'same source → same deal' also gives the same code, and the test can't tell the two apart. Also, assignSources reduces the seed to 32 bits (`seed >>> 0`), so different injected values can collapse to the same seed. The test has to check that its two seeds give different deals after that reduction, which the plan already asks for. Finally, spying on node:crypto's randomInt only works with vi.mock hoisting. vi.spyOn on an ESM namespace fails.
concerns.consequence: The test can pass while the deal still depends on the match code, or the spy approach can fail at typecheck or at runtime and cost rework.

concerns.message: The new integration tests add room time: the guest collects both types (two 6 s channels unless the rules are overridden), and the seed test builds at least three rooms. The snapshot's integration duration isn't recorded here, and the acceptance says the suite must stay 'well inside' its budget.
concerns.consequence: Without the collection-time overrides the suite may drift toward the 300 s check timeout. The worker then has to retrofit overrides or parallelism late in the run.

simpler_alternative: Keep the plan, with two changes. In theft-loop, treat settlement.choice === 'winner' (shown as the host's 'You chose …' notice) as the proof that the click happened before the deadline, because only chooseTheft can produce that value. Measure the margin as settlement.tick minus the tick the window opened, and require it to be at most 40 ticks, which is the same as being at least 60 ticks before the deadline. Read it from room diagnostics, and don't add protocol fields just for the test. For the seed, inject a plain `() => number` seed source into the room, used only for the ledger. The room test calls assignSources with the chosen seeds to confirm the deals differ, then checks that the room's sources match assignSources(sites, source()) whatever the match code.
cheap_experiment: Right after restoring the snapshot, before other changes: (1) grep the e2e server entry and test settings for theftChoiceTicks and other rule overrides, to confirm the browser server keeps the 100-tick window; (2) add a temporary click on the single option to theft-loop and log the window-open tick, settlement.tick and choiceDeadline from room diagnostics over 5 runs on this machine. If the worst-case margin is well above 60 ticks, keep the plan. If not, move the choice UI in front of the result banner or transition first.
